clue.text: Establishment job with service to stamp-collectors

parts.note: a post is a job or position of employment
an office is a religious service, as in the Divine Office

explanation.surface: A firm offers a job providing a service to philatelists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with service to stamp-collectors' doubles as a hint: philatelists buy their stamps across this counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A national postal organisation is an institution, an establishment in the formal sense.

clue.text: Writer renamed E Anglian river

definitions.meaning: the pen name of the novelist Eric Blair, author of 1984
a river in Suffolk, East Anglia, flowing into the sea at Felixstowe

explanation.walkthrough: 'renamed' links the two: Eric Blair took his pen name from the Suffolk river.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Eric Blair chose a pseudonym borrowed from a Suffolk river he loved.

clue.text: Materials for tea with staff, members

indicators.note: the members of a word are its constituent letters, so the letters of tea and staff are reassembled

explanation.surface: Cloth bought for a tea party held with the office workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' tells you to take the letters that make up TEA and STAFF and rebuild them, giving a shiny fabric in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp silk or rayon fabric, so the plural names kinds of cloth.

clue.text: Looks to Gavin perhaps 'to avoid shame

parts.note: looks, as in expressions, are faces

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the name could be a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone appears to Gavin as a way of escaping humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'to' is a print artefact; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal, and 'to avoid shame' works as an adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A face-saving move preserves dignity and prevents humiliation.

clue.text: Orders measures to circumvent depression

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: inches, abbreviated INS, are measures of length
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Instructions about measuring to get round an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: In commerce an indent is an official order for goods, especially from abroad.

clue.text: So hesitant a dismissal?

parts.note: er is the sound of a hesitant speaker
go! is a curt dismissal

explanation.surface: Is that an uncertain way of telling someone to leave?
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used in English to draw a conclusion.

clue.text: First baron previously made court poet

definitions.text: First baron previously made court poet

parts.words: First baron previously made court poet
parts.note: the Victorian Poet Laureate who was appointed to the court post in 1850 and only later raised to the peerage as the first holder of his barony

explanation.walkthrough: The 'court poet' is the Poet Laureate; the title 'Baron' came in 1884, decades after the laureateship.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of In Memoriam was Poet Laureate before becoming the first baron of his line.

clue.text: Fresh start made with can opener and thin rope

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lean means thin
a sheet is a sailing rope controlling a sail

explanation.surface: A new beginning achieved using a tin-opener and some slender cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can opener' looks like a kitchen tool but gives the first letter of 'can'; a SHEET is a nautical rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean sheet is an unblemished record, a chance to begin afresh.

clue.text: Display on the subject of meat

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: An exhibition about butchery.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to show or disclose it.

clue.text: Coming or going ? Hard to say with one so false

parts.words: Coming or going ? Hard to say with one so
parts.note: a figure with a face on each side, like Janus, could be heading either way, so you cannot tell

explanation.surface: Someone so confused you cannot tell if they are arriving or leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocrite shows one face and hides another, so is deceitful.

clue.text: The number one craze

parts.note: looking after number one means caring for oneself, the ego
a mania is a craze

explanation.surface: The fad that is top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessive self-regard is a passion for one's own self.

clue.text: Scheme for US car park

definitions.meaning: a piece of ground, like an American parking lot

explanation.definitionFit: A plan or conspiracy; also a small piece of ground, which Americans would call a lot for parking.

clue.text: Hieroglyphs of no little weight among ancient Britons

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Picts were ancient inhabitants of northern Britain
O, the figure nought, stands for no
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Symbols of no significance found among early Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieroglyphs are picture symbols standing for words or ideas.

clue.text: Isn't his tea awful? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: awful suggests the words are a mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A guest protests that the brew is horrible, and is contradicted.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact opposite is the direct contrary of something.

clue.text: Irritability the contact man may cause ?

parts.note: a person who touches others might be expected to produce the state named, punning on touch

explanation.surface: A go-between may provoke annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easily offended is a sensitive, prickly temper.

clue.text: So bitter it may be taken with soda

definitions.text: it may be taken with soda

explanation.surface: A drink so sharp it needs a splash of soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting or sarcastic remarks; also the adjective that precedes soda in the name of a corrosive chemical.

clue.text: Indian state fixing meeting on modernization

parts.note: UP is Uttar Pradesh, a state of India
dating is fixing the date of a meeting

explanation.surface: A regional government arranging a conference on modernising.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing something up to date is modernising it.

clue.text: Knows, I hear, slangy US comedian

parts.note: knows sounds like nose, and the slang nickname Schnozzola for a big nose belonged to this American entertainer

explanation.surface: An American comic who is wise to street slang.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Durante was famous for his large nose, nicknamed 'the Schnozzola'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Durante was a celebrated American vaudeville and film comic.

clue.text: Demolished a Lancing church

indicators.note: something demolished is broken up, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A chapel at Lancing College was knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancing is a town and public school in Sussex with a famous chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England and its sister churches form the Anglican communion.

clue.text: The past was a blank for Viola

definitions.meaning: in Twelfth Night, Viola says her sister's story was 'A blank, my lord'

explanation.definitionFit: Bygone events; also Viola's word when asked about her imaginary sister's life story.

clue.text: Not our modern type of speech

definitions.text: Not our modern type of speech

parts.words: Not our modern type of speech
parts.note: the language of the Anglo-Saxons, also the name of a gothic typeface, hence type

explanation.definitionFit: The ancestor of present-day English, spoken before the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: Have a shot at ibex

parts.note: to have a go is to have a shot

explanation.surface: A hunter takes aim at a mountain animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain species of the same family as sheep.

clue.text: State request in another's name briefly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
briefly shortens the word by dropping letters

parts.note: an alias is a name taken from another identity
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A petition filed under somebody else's name, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' here drops two letters from the middle and end of the name word, an old-style loose shortening; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest US state, bought from Russia in 1867.

clue.text: Work, in a backward way, to crater formation

indicators.note: formation suggests the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Labouring backwards to shape a crater.
explanation.definitionFit: To act retrospectively is to have effect on past events.

clue.text: The unbounded East, 'and India's boundaries

indicators.note: unbounded means without its outer letters
the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The vast East and the borders of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent is the East, and India lies within its bounds.

clue.text: No enclosure found ? Mine's on top

parts.note: open land has no enclosure
to found metal is to cast it

explanation.surface: No fence discovered: my land is on high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Surface mining digs from the top rather than through shafts.

clue.text: Indian language-teacher. Numbers returned to his new form

parts.note: Num. is the abbreviation of the Book of Numbers

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tutor in India sends sums back to a pupil to redo.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a munshi was a secretary or interpreter who taught languages.

clue.text: African like Coleridge's dulcimer-playing damsel

definitions.meaning: in Kubla Khan, 'It was an ... maid, And on her dulcimer she played'

explanation.definitionFit: A native of old Ethiopia; also the nationality of the maid in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan.
